'''''Viola arborescens''''' is a species of ''[[Viola (plant)|Viola]]'' and is also known as the '''tree violet'''.<ref name=rhshd>{{ cite web |url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/horticulturaldatabase/hortdatabase.asp?ID=49597 |title=''Viola arborescens'' |work=RHS Horticultural Database |publisher=[[Royal Horticultural Society]] |access-date=August 21, 2011}}</ref> The average height is anywhere from 8 to 10 inches. ''Viola arborescens'' requires direct sunlight to grow. ''Viola arborescens'' is very cold hardy, and is in bloom all winter and into early spring.

[[Image:Viola arborescens03022002.JPG|150px|thumb|left]]

==Color==
The ''Viola arborescens'' displays color all winter and into early spring. Typical natural colors include magenta, gold, light blue, dark purple, maroon and off-white.

==Distribution==
''Viola arborescens'' is native to the western [[Mediterranean Basin]]. It is found in southern France, Sardinia and the Balearic Islands, eastern and southern Spain, southwestern Portugal (around the [[Sagres Point]]), Morocco and Algeria.
